mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate earnings, thus driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates a weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and thus leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS MoM < -5% and 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points month-over-month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE MoM > 0.5pp and 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which is typically associated with economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO MoM > 1% and 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points within a month signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS MoM < -0.25% and 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points month-over-month signals a strengthening demand side and a tightening labor market, which typically leads to economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST MoM > 0 & UNRATE MoM < -0.5pp and 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months and 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a tightening monetary policy (FEDFUNDS) signals a potential economic slowdown, as higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer purchasing power lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% & FEDFUNDS > 2% and 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.
